sn45.8:1.2: See note on [sn12.2:1.2]() for a discussion of “analysis” discourses.
sn45.8:3.1: “View” (_diṭṭhi_, Sanskrit _dṛṣṭi_) is “seeing” and hence a term for “understanding” (Aitareya Upaniṣad 3.2). In Buddhism, it means a particular way of seeing or perspective, a theory or view through which one makes sense of the world. By itself it is neutral, although “views” in plural sometimes stands for the thicket of wrong views.
sn45.8:4.1: _Saṅkappa_ may be rendered with “thought” ([sn14.8:3.3](), [mn60:24.2]()), “intention” ([mn41:14.3]()), “resolve”, or “purpose”. It has a directionality to it: in Rig Veda 10.164.5 it is the “evil intent” wished upon those who we hate, whereas in Atharva Veda 3.25.2 it is a quality of the arrow of love.
sn45.8:5.2: The factors of speech and action are defined in detail at [mn27:13.4]().
sn45.8:7.2: Wrong livelihood is defined at [mn117:29.2]() and [an5.177:1.3]().
